title: Disability employment-population ratio, July 2026
question: What will BLS first report for the not seasonally adjusted employment-population ratio for people with a disability, 16 years and over, in July 2026?
resolutionSource: U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics Employment Situation, Table A-6
resolutionRule: Resolves to the first BLS Employment Situation Table A-6 print released on Aug. 7, 2026 for July 2026, employment-population ratio for people with a disability, total 16 years and over, not seasonally adjusted, in percent, rounded to one decimal. The rolling BLS Table A-6 URL is the official table location; resolution should capture the Aug. 7, 2026 first-print artifact when released. Later revisions or historical database updates do not change resolution.
drivers: Recent disability EPOP drift lower in early 2026
July non-seasonally-adjusted month effect usually slightly negative from June
Soft June labor market and lower overall participation
High month-to-month CPS sampling noise for disability subgroup

reasoning.text: Framing and exact resolver: this forecast targets BLS CPS series LNU02374597, Employment-Population Ratio - With a Disability, 16 Years and over, not seasonally adjusted, as printed in Employment Situation Table A-6 for July 2026. FRED is used only as a public history mirror; BLS Table A-6 is the resolution source.

reasoning.call: BLS release schedule lookup for Employment Situation July 2026 reference month
reasoning.result: BLS schedule lists July 2026 Employment Situation release date as Aug. 07, 2026 at 08:30 AM.

reasoning.call: FRED mirror of BLS LNU02374597 recent monthly observations
reasoning.result: LNU02374597 values fetched: Feb 2026 22.4, Mar 2026 22.2, Apr 2026 21.8, May 2026 21.7, Jun 2026 21.8; units percent, not seasonally adjusted.

reasoning.text: Reference class and base rate: for this not seasonally adjusted level series, persistence from the latest official print is the base rate, so the starting prior is Jun 2026 at 21.8. The July target uses the same variant as the anchors: total people with a disability, age 16 years and over, not seasonally adjusted, percent.

reasoning.call: BLS Employment Situation Table A-6 June 2026 latest official table
reasoning.result: Table A-6 shows total people with a disability employment-population ratio of 22.7 in June 2025 and 21.8 in June 2026; employed people with a disability were 8,081 thousand in June 2025 and 8,054 thousand in June 2026.

reasoning.call: BLS June 2026 Employment Situation labor-market context
reasoning.result: June 2026 nonfarm payrolls were +57,000, unemployment rate was 4.2 percent, labor force participation decreased 0.3 percentage point to 61.5 percent, and overall employment-population ratio edged down 0.2 percentage point to 59.0 percent.

reasoning.text: Prior/update/interval: persistence prior is Jun 2026 at 21.8. Historical sample is monthly LNU02374597 values from Jan 2024 through Jun 2026, excluding the missing Oct 2025 observation; successive-change dispersion gives sigma = 0.528 percentage point, so 1.28*sigma = 0.676. Adjustment components are -0.1 point for recent 2026 downward level drift, -0.1 point for typical Jun-to-Jul NSA softness, and 0.0 point for mixed labor-market context, implying 21.8 - 0.2 = 21.6. The 80% interval is 21.6 +/- 0.7, rounded to [20.9, 22.3].
Momentum: the series moved 22.6, 22.4, 22.2, 21.8, 21.7, 21.8 from Jan through Jun 2026, so the latest uptick is small relative to the earlier slide and does not fully erase the weaker level.

Counter-consideration: upside risk is a rebound in disability labor-force attachment or CPS sampling that would land above the interval, roughly 22.4 or higher; downside risk is another broad participation drop or subgroup sampling swing that would land below the interval, roughly 20.8 or lower.
